 Judgment

This appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (the Act) has been filed by the claim petitioner in O.P.(MV) No.260/2017 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal,
Perumbavoor, (the Tribunal), aggrieved by the amount of compensation granted by Award dated 29/07/2019.
The sole respondent herein is the third respondent in the petition.
In this appeal, the parties and the documents will be referred to as described in the original petition.

2. According to the claim petitioner, on 19/11/2016 at about 08:00 p.m., while he was pillion riding on motorcycle bearing registration No.KL-48/A-4780 through the Aluva-Munnar road and when he reached the place by name Odakkali, pick-up van bearing registration No.TN-60/Q-4738 driven by the second respondent in a rash and negligent manner knocked him down as a result of which he 2025:KER:66458 sustained grievous injuries.
An amount of 25,00,000/- was claimed as compensation under various heads.
3. The first respondent/owner and the second respondent/driver filed written statement denying negligence on the part of the second respondent/driver and the claims under various heads.
4. The third respondent/insurer filed written statement admitting the policy, but denying negligence on the part of the second respondent/driver of the offending vehicle.
The amount of compensation claimed under various heads were disputed.
5. Before the Tribunal, PW1 was examined and Exts.A11 to A19 were marked on the side of the claim petitioner.
No oral or documentary evidence was produced by the respondents.
Ext.C1 was also marked.

6. The Tribunal on consideration of the oral and documentary evidence and after hearing both sides,
found negligence on the part of the second respondent/driver of the offending vehicle resulting in the incident and hence awarded an amount of 17,58,321/- together with interest @ 8% per annum from the date of the petition till the date of 2025:KER:66458 realisation with proportionate costs.
Aggrieved by the Award, the claim petitioner has come up in appeal.
7. The only point that arises for consideration in this appeal is whether there is any infirmity in the findings of the Tribunal calling for an interference by this Court.

sentences.text: 9. The award of compensation by the Tribunal under the following heads is challenged by the claim petitioner- Notional income

It is submitted by the learned counsel for the claim petitioner that in the connected appeal, that is, MACA No.619/2020, the notional income of the claim petitioner therein was fixed at 17,000/- per month.
Therefore, the notional income of the claim petitioner in this case may also be fixed at 17,000/- per month.
The Tribunal by the impugned Award disposed of two claim petitions, viz., O.P.(MV)No.196/2017 and O.P.(MV)No.260/2017.
The claim petitioners in O.P.(MV)No.196/2017 are the legal heirs of one Akshay Gopi who was riding the motor bike on which the claim petitioner herein was the pillion rider.
The deceased in the said case 2025:KER:66458 was also an Engineering student.
MACA No.619/2020 filed by the claim petitioners in O.P.(MV)No.196/2017, was disposed of by this Court by judgment dated 20/06/2025.
The notional income was fixed at 17,000/-.
Hence the notional income of the claim petitioner herein is also fixed as 17,000/-.
Pain and suffering 10.

The materials on record show that the claim petitioner sustained the following injuries-  Type 3 open comminuted supracondylar - intercondyalr fracture right femur with bone defect  Type 3 open fracture patella-Right
Closed comminuted fracture both bones right leg M/3 rd - L/3rd  Fracture both bones - radius / ulna - Right forearm with crush injury right hand and forearm  Fracture base of P1 right index finger
Fracture shaft of P1 right middle finger
Fracture head of 2nd , and 3rd metacarpals right
PIO joint dislocation right little finger
Right temporal SAH and hematoma
Linear undisplaced fracture of the left parietal bone He was hospitalized for a period of 30 days.
The materials on record 2025:KER:66458 show that he sustained about 12 fractures and he had underwent 5 surgeries.
Hence, in the facts and circumstances of the case, an amount of 1,85,000/- is awarded under this head.
Loss of amenities 11.
In the facts and circumstances of the case, an amount of 1,85,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.
Addition to be made towards future prospects 12.
The claim petitioner was a 20 year old student at the time of the accident and therefore 40% of his income is liable to be added towards his established income.
